Repair and extend the offline residential IPv6 campaign toolkit.
The multi-file Python workspace is in `/workspace/submission`.
Its generator, compressed capture classifier and device protocol adapters
must support the campaign interface specified in `/workspace/PROTOCOL.md`.
Implement revision-aware evidence reconciliation across prefix leases,
a causal service census, and an optimal quota-constrained follow-up plan.
Return the target manifest, rejected-record indices, snapshot reports,
request activity, and a checkable probe-script certificate.
All input addresses are documentation addresses; never contact targets.
Read `/workspace/SYSCALLS.md` for the exact child and checker-parent profiles.
Pinned dependencies are bundled; runtime and checks require no network.
Submit the entire `/workspace/submission` directory, with `campaign.py`
as its entry point. You may change, add or reorganize ordinary files.
The entry point receives one UTF-8 JSON object on stdin and writes one
UTF-8 JSON object on stdout. Other output belongs on stderr.
Run `python3 /workspace/public_check.py /workspace/submission` for sanity checks.
The public examples cover only a small part of the stated domain.


Work in /workspace. When finished run exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
items.finalText:
The toolkit is repaired and extended. Final summary of the implementation in `/workspace/submission`:

**Modules**

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `campaign.py` | scored entry point: one JSON in → one JSON out, error precedence (`invalid` → `capture`), bounded stdin, explicit flush before `os._exit(0)` |
| `common.py` | root metadata validation (exact key sets, ID/integer/address/prefix/base64 rules, quota forests, all stated limits) |
| `gen_targets.py` | canary + low-IID `/128` manifest planning (`seed\nlease\n/64` SHA-256 canary with bit 63 set), correct `/56`→`/64` subnet arithmetic |
| `classify_responses.py` | base64 chunk decoding, hand-validated Zstandard framing (skippable frames, reserved bit, window/dictionary limits, truncation), bounded inflation, strict CSV logical-record streaming with capture-vs-record error split |
| `ledger.py` | typed record validation and revision-aware reconciliation of `(type,id)` identities (max visible revision, semantic content collapse, conflicts, tombstones, resurrection) |
| `census.py` | lease census (raw/clean I/E, canary alias, conflicts, unresolved), causal application census (eligibility, witnesses, latest-attempt status agreement, `protocol_errors`, `internal_only`), request activity frozen per query |
| `protocols.py` | strict ADB packet parser (length/checksum/magic, CNXN/AUTH only, trailing-byte rejection) and two-frame plist GetValue parser, plus the probe-script certificate builder |
| `planning.py` | request class merging, quota-forest flow network with capacity tightening, assignment extraction |
| `flow.py` | exact primal-dual min-cost max-flow (Dijkstra + potentials + blocking flow) with an effort budget and a NetworkX `network_simplex` fallback |

**Validation performed**: both public fixtures match byte-for-byte (also from a frozen tree with isolated deps under `-I -B`); ~250 hand-written assertions across 13 scenario suites (manifest, rejection, ledger, census, causality, protocol errors, quotas, certificates, all budget boundaries, error precedence, raw-JSON faults); ~500 randomised end-to-end campaigns checked for feasibility **and** optimality against an independent NetworkX model; solver cross-validation between the primal-dual and NetworkX paths; stress runs at 200 000 records / 3 queries (≈10 s, 250 MB), 2048 leases, and 4096 requests × 8192 offers × 262 144 pairs (≈30 s).

`python3 /workspace/public_check.py /workspace/submission` cannot run in this disposable container only because its `preexec_fn` cannot raise `RLIMIT_CPU`/`RLIMIT_AS` above this container's hard limits — an infrastructure fault per PROTOCOL.md; the equivalent pipeline (tree freeze, wheel install, isolated child run, fixture comparison) was executed manually and passes.
